_about: Offline pest knowledge base for the 102 IP102 pest classes, organised into management groups. Doses are common Indian extension recommendations for knapsack sprays (per litre of water). Always follow the product label and local KVK advice.

aphids.name: Aphids
aphids.damage: Suck sap from tender shoots and leaves; curling, yellowing, sticky honeydew and sooty mould; some spread viruses.
organic: Strong water spray on small plants
aphids.threshold: Spray only when colonies are on many shoots and natural enemies are few.

planthoppers.name: Planthoppers
planthoppers.damage: Suck sap at the base of rice tillers; plants yellow and dry in circular patches ('hopper burn').
cultural: Alternate wetting and drying; drain the field for 3-4 days
Leave 30 cm alleys every 2-3 m for air flow
organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L directed at the plant base
chemical: Spray at the base of the plants; avoid synthetic pyrethroids (they cause resurgence)

leafhoppers_bugs.name: Leafhoppers, plant bugs and lanternflies
leafhoppers_bugs.damage: Suck sap from leaves, flowers and young fruit; leaf edges yellow or burn, flowers and fruitlets drop.
chemical: On mango, spray at panicle emergence, not during full bloom, to protect pollinators
leafhoppers_bugs.threshold: Spray when many insects are seen per shoot or panicle.

stem_borers.name: Stem and shoot borers
stem_borers.damage: Larvae bore into stems or shoots; central shoot dries ('dead heart'), panicles turn white and empty ('white ear'), shoots wilt.
cultural: Clip leaf tips of rice seedlings before transplanting (removes egg masses)
Harvest close to the ground and destroy stubble
organic: Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids (1 card, 20,000 eggs per acre) weekly
chemical: Cartap hydrochloride 4 G granules 10 kg per acre in standing water (rice)
stem_borers.threshold: Rice: 5% dead hearts or 1 egg mass per square metre.

caterpillars.name: Leaf-eating caterpillars, armyworms and cutworms
caterpillars.damage: Larvae eat leaves, fold leaves, cut seedlings at the base or bore into cobs and fruit.
cultural: Hand-pick and destroy larvae and egg masses
Cutworms: flood irrigation and evening scouting at the plant base
organic: Maize whorl: apply sand mixed with lime
chemical: Spinetoram 11.7 SC 0.5 ml/L (fall armyworm in maize)
caterpillars.threshold: Spray when young larvae are found on 10% of plants; young larvae are much easier to control.

beetles_weevils.name: Beetles and weevils
beetles_weevils.damage: Adults chew holes in leaves, flowers or fruit; some larvae feed on roots, seeds or inside fruit.
cultural: Collect and destroy fallen fruit (mango weevils)
Blister beetles: use gloves, the body fluid blisters skin
beetles_weevils.threshold: Spray when many leaves or flowers are being damaged.

soil_pests.name: Soil pests (white grubs, wireworms, mole crickets, chafers)
soil_pests.damage: Feed on roots and underground stems; plants wilt and die in patches; seedlings cut below the soil.
cultural: Collect adult beetles at light traps after the first rains
organic: Neem cake 100 kg per acre at sowing
Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria bassiana mixed with manure
chemical: Use a soil insecticide recommended by your local KVK at sowing
soil_pests.threshold: Act when patches of wilting plants with damaged roots are found.

mites.name: Mites
mites.damage: Tiny pests on the leaf underside; speckling, bronzing, curling, galls or felt-like patches; fine webbing.
cultural: Avoid pyrethroids that kill predatory mites
mites.threshold: Spray when speckling spreads to many leaves.

thrips.name: Thrips
thrips.damage: Rasp and suck leaves and flowers; silvery streaks, upward or downward curling, scarred fruit.
thrips.threshold: Spray when curling or silvering appears on new growth.

whiteflies.name: Whiteflies and blackflies
whiteflies.damage: Suck sap from the leaf underside; yellowing, honeydew and sooty mould; spread leaf curl viruses.
cultural: Remove infested lower leaves and weeds
whiteflies.threshold: Spray when adults are seen on most leaves.

scales_mealybugs.name: Scale insects and mealybugs
scales_mealybugs.damage: Sessile sap-suckers on twigs, leaves and fruit; yellowing, twig dieback, honeydew and sooty mould.
cultural: Prune and burn heavily infested twigs
Control ants that protect them (band trunks with sticky material)
Release the ladybird Cryptolaemus montrouzieri (mealybugs) or Rodolia (cottony cushion scale)
chemical: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.3 ml/L for heavy infestations
scales_mealybugs.threshold: Treat when colonies cover twigs or fruit.

fruit_flies.name: Fruit flies
fruit_flies.damage: Maggots feed inside fruit; fruit rots and drops early.
cultural: Collect fallen and infested fruit every few days and bury deeply (60 cm)
organic: Bait spray: protein hydrolysate or jaggery bait with a recommended insecticide, applied in spots
chemical: Use a bait spray recommended by your local KVK; avoid cover sprays close to harvest

gall_midges_flies.name: Gall midges, stem maggots and leaf-miner flies
gall_midges_flies.damage: Maggots form galls, mine leaves or feed inside stems and flowers; silver shoots ('onion leaf') in rice, mined or galled leaves.
cultural: Remove and destroy galled or mined leaves and shoots
organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L at early infestation
chemical: Thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.3 g/L or a locally recommended insecticide at the early stage
Leaf miners: Spinosad 45 SC 0.3 ml/L or Abamectin 1.9 EC 0.5 ml/L
gall_midges_flies.threshold: Act early; once galls or mines are formed, sprays are less effective.

tree_borers.name: Trunk and branch borers
tree_borers.damage: Larvae tunnel inside trunks and branches; sawdust-like frass, gum, wilting branches, tree decline.
cultural: Keep the trunk clean; remove loose bark
Kill larvae in holes with a wire
organic: Plug cleaned holes with mud after killing larvae
chemical: Plug holes with cotton soaked in an insecticide recommended by your local KVK, then seal with mud
tree_borers.threshold: Inspect trunks regularly for fresh frass.

locusts_grasshoppers.name: Locusts and grasshoppers
locusts_grasshoppers.damage: Chew leaves and stems; swarms can destroy whole fields.
cultural: Plough field borders to destroy egg pods
Report swarms immediately to the Locust Warning Organisation / agriculture department
chemical: Swarm control is done by government teams; do not spray swarms on your own

phylloxera.name: Grape phylloxera
phylloxera.damage: Aphid-like insect forming galls on leaves and roots; root feeding weakens and kills vines.
cultural: Clean tools and boots between vineyards
organic: No effective organic control for root forms
chemical: Leaf galls: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL 0.3 ml/L at early gall formation
phylloxera.threshold: Plant resistant rootstocks; treat leaf galls only when they are numerous.
